parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional retry key (use a fresh UUID per logical create). If a bot was already created for your account with this key, the API skips creation and replays that bot with HTTP 507. Keys do not expire. A failed create is not cached, so a retry after a failure runs fresh.

200.description: Deduplication replay. A bot already exists for this `deduplication_key` and the same `meeting_link`; it is returned instead of creating a new one.

400.description: Invalid request body (wrong field type, invalid meeting link, unsupported option for the platform, invalid `agent_config_id`, `join_at` in the past). Since November 2026 these also return 400: `audio_required` and `video_required` both `false` with nothing else for the bot to do; `video_separate_streams: true` without `video_required: true` on Google Meet or Microsoft Teams; a `bot_image_url` that is not an `https://` image URL; a Zoom link with no meeting number (for example a personal `/my/` link); and `meeting_captions` on a Zoom bot that uses your own Zoom app.

401.description: The key is not a workspace API key. Send a workspace key as `Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY`.

403.description: Missing or invalid API key, insufficient credits, or the account cannot create bots.

404.description: A resource named in the request was not found, for example a `teams.sign_in_email` that is not registered under `teams.teams_login_domain`.

409.description: The `deduplication_key` is already bound to a bot for a different meeting.

422.description: MIA agents are not offered in your workspace's execution region. Create the bot without `agent_config_id`, or contact support.

429.description: Prepaid account bot-creation limit exceeded (5 per minute or 50 per hour for immediate and near-term bots), or no signed-in login is available. No bot is created. Bot creation rate-limit responses include the `Retry-After` header (seconds) and `limit`, `window` (minute or hour) and `retry_after` in the body. Wait that many seconds before you retry, or set `join_at` at least 10 minutes ahead: those bots do not count.

500.description: Server error. Retry with exponential backoff and the same `Idempotency-Key`.

503.description: The service or region for this request is not ready. Retry with backoff.

507.description: Idempotent replay, not an error. A bot was already created with this `Idempotency-Key`; its id, meeting URL and current status are returned and no new bot is created.

post.description:
Temporarily pauses capture for a bot that is in a Google Meet, Zoom or Microsoft Teams meeting.
The bot remains in the meeting, but recorded and streamed video becomes black, audio becomes
silent, and real-time transcription stops producing words. The recording timeline is preserved.

Pausing a bot that is already paused changes nothing and returns `409` with `"status": "no_op"`
and `"recording_paused": true`, so you can tell that no change was made.

parameters.name: bot_id
parameters.description: The ID returned when the bot was created.

403.description: Missing or invalid API key, or the bot belongs to another account.

409.description: No change was made. Recording is already paused (`"status": "no_op"`, `"recording_paused": true`), or the bot is not in the meeting (the body includes `bot_status`).

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. This endpoint allows 30 requests per minute per bot.

503.description: The bot is not currently recording or is unreachable.

post.description:
Resumes normal video, audio, stream, and real-time transcription capture for a paused bot
in a Google Meet, Zoom or Microsoft Teams meeting. The recording continues on the original
timeline.

Resuming a bot that is already recording changes nothing and returns `409` with
`"status": "no_op"` and `"recording_paused": false`, so you can tell that no change was made.

post.description:
Send a command to a bot that is in a live meeting. Use `raise_hand` to raise the bot's hand,
`lower_hand` to lower it, or `screenshot` to capture the meeting. Hand commands use the meeting's
own raise-hand control, so everyone in the meeting sees the change. Screenshots are supported
on Google Meet and Teams; Zoom bots that join through your Zoom app (Meeting SDK) do not
support them. Retrieve captures with Get Bot Screenshots.

For hand commands, the response includes `hand_raised`: the hand state the bot read back from
the meeting after it acted. A repeated hand command changes nothing and returns `200` with the
current state. `hand_raised` does not apply to `screenshot`.

Supported on Google Meet, Zoom and Microsoft Teams. The bot must be in the meeting (status
`InMeeting`, `Recording` or `RecordingPermissionAllowed`). Allow up to 10 seconds for a response.
Shares the 30 requests per minute per bot limit with the other in-meeting commands. See the
[Raise & Lower Hand guide](/guides/features/raise-lower-hand).

parameters.name: bot_id
parameters.description: The ID returned when the bot was created.

200.description: The bot accepted the command. Hand commands include `hand_raised`, the hand state after the command.

use_own_app.description: True uses your connected Zoom app and requires one. False joins without your Zoom app or credentials and cannot be combined with zak_url or obf_url. Omit or send null to use your app when connected and otherwise join without one. The field is omitted from bot details.

zak_url.description: HTTPS mint URL returning a ZAK to join as a signed-in Zoom user. Mutually exclusive with obf_url.

obf_url.description: HTTPS mint URL returning a fresh, single-use OBF token at join time. Parent must already be in the meeting; bot is removed when parent leaves. Do not include meeting_number; MeetStream appends it. Mutually exclusive with zak_url.

CreateBotRequestZoom.description: Optionally set use_own_app to true to require your connected Zoom app, or false to join without your app or credentials. When omitted or null, your app is used if connected or your Zoom credentials are saved; otherwise the bot joins without one. If Zoom refuses your app, the bot does not try again without it. Joining without your app is not available in every region: there, use_own_app false returns 400 `Zoom bots are not available in this region right now`, and an omitted use_own_app needs your app. For authenticated Zoom join, send exactly one of zak_url or obf_url, optionally with use_own_app true. Neither URL works with use_own_app false. MeetStream fetches your HTTPS mint URL at join time; your server owns OAuth and refresh tokens. Fetch failure does not fall back to a guest join. Both URLs together return 400. The deprecated fields use_zoom_obf and zoom_oauth_connection_user_id are rejected. See /guides/app-integrations/zoom-authenticated-bots.
CreateBotRequestZoom.title: CreateBotRequestZoom

A `teams` block with a wrong type or a missing required field returns `400` with a message that names the field. Sending `teams` for a non-Teams link also returns `400`. See /guides/app-integrations/teams-signed-in-bots.

matches.description: Case-insensitive substrings. A participant counts as a bot when their display name contains any of them.

AutomaticLeaveConfigBotDetection.description: Leave when every remaining participant looks like another notetaker bot. Opt-in; only the `using_participant_names` mechanism is supported and other keys are rejected with 400.
AutomaticLeaveConfigBotDetection.title: AutomaticLeaveConfigBotDetection

waiting_room_timeout.description: Seconds to wait in the waiting room before leaving. 60 to 600 on Google Meet, 60 to 1200 on Zoom, 60 to 1800 on Microsoft Teams. Default 600 (1200 on Teams).

no_one_joined_timeout.description: Seconds to stay in an empty meeting, waiting for the first other participant to join. 60 to 1800. Default 600 (1200 on Teams).

everyone_left_timeout.description: Seconds to stay after everyone else leaves. 60 to 1800. Default 600 (1200 on Teams).

voice_inactivity_timeout.description: Seconds without speech before the bot leaves. 60 to 1800. Default 600.

in_call_recording_timeout.description: Maximum seconds to stay in the call while recording. 600 to 18000. Default 14400 (4 hours).

recording_permission_denied_timeout.description: Zoom only. Seconds to wait for the host to answer the bot's recording request before the bot leaves. 60 to 600. Default 600.

bot_detection.description: Leave when every remaining participant looks like another notetaker bot. Opt-in; only the `using_participant_names` mechanism is supported and other keys are rejected with 400.

AutomaticLeaveConfig.description: Configure how long the bot should remain in the meeting under different conditions before leaving automatically. All timeout values are specified in seconds and accept integer values only.

RecordingConfigVideoLayout.description: Layout used for the composited meeting video. `speaker_view` follows the active speaker, which is usually what you want for review and clipping. `grid_view` is a composited mosaic of everyone in the call. The API defaults to `grid_view` when video is recorded and this field is omitted, so send `speaker_view` explicitly when you want it. Ignored unless `video_required` is true, because an audio-only bot never runs the compositor. Supported on Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and Zoom. Google Meet and Microsoft Teams also accept `grid_view_default` and `speaker_view_default`: the bot records the meeting's own grid or speaker view during the call, as one finished file. Zoom accepts only `grid_view` and `speaker_view`. WhatsApp supports only `grid_view`.

meeting_link.description: The URL of the Google Meet, Zoom, or Teams meeting.

bot_name.description: The display name the bot uses in the meeting. Defaults to `MeetStream`. On some platforms only letters, numbers, spaces and `- ' . _ @` are accepted.

storage_id.description: The ID of a storage destination that you created in the dashboard: 1 to 80 letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens. Omit it to use your workspace's default destination, or MeetStream storage when you have none. An ID in the wrong format, an unknown ID, or a destination that fails its access check returns 400. If the check cannot run, the request returns 503; retry it.

audio_required.description: Whether the bot records the mixed meeting audio. Must be true when `audio_mixed_mp3` is true.

video_required.description: Whether the bot records meeting video. Defaults to `false`, so the bot records audio only. Send `true` to record video. Audio-only bots process faster and use less storage, and transcripts, diarization and speaker timelines all work without video. When video is on, set `recording_config.video_layout` to `speaker_view` to follow the active speaker. The default layout is `grid_view`.

audio_mixed_mp3.description: Also produce an MP3 copy of the mixed meeting audio, returned as `audio_mp3_url` by Get Bot Audio. Requires `audio_required: true`. Can also be set inside `recording_config`; the top-level value wins when both are sent.

audio_separate_mp3.description: Also produce MP3 copies of each per-participant audio segment, returned as `download_url_mp3` by Get Audio Streams. Requires `audio_separate_streams: true`. Can also be set inside `recording_config`.

deduplication_key.description: Your own logical key for this bot (printable ASCII, 1-2000 characters). It is bound permanently to the first bot created with it for your account. Sending the same key again returns that existing bot with HTTP 200 instead of creating a new one; sending it with a different `meeting_link` returns 409. Use the `Idempotency-Key` header instead for transport-level retries. See the Deduplication & Idempotency Keys guide.

initial_audio.description: A one-shot audio clip the bot plays into the meeting shortly after it is admitted. Google Meet and Microsoft Teams. A Zoom bot that joins through your Zoom app returns 400.

agent_config_params.description: Values for the template variables in the MIA agent's system prompt, for this bot only. Keys are variable names; values must be strings or primitives (objects and arrays are rejected). Used with `agent_config_id`.

zoom.description: Optionally set use_own_app to true to require your connected Zoom app, or false to join without your app or credentials. When omitted or null, your app is used if connected or your Zoom credentials are saved; otherwise the bot joins without one. If Zoom refuses your app, the bot does not try again without it. Joining without your app is not available in every region: there, use_own_app false returns 400 `Zoom bots are not available in this region right now`, and an omitted use_own_app needs your app. For authenticated Zoom join, send exactly one of zak_url or obf_url, optionally with use_own_app true. Neither URL works with use_own_app false. MeetStream fetches your HTTPS mint URL at join time; your server owns OAuth and refresh tokens. Fetch failure does not fall back to a guest join. Both URLs together return 400. The deprecated fields use_zoom_obf and zoom_oauth_connection_user_id are rejected. See /guides/app-integrations/zoom-authenticated-bots.

video_separate_streams.description: Record one video file for each participant, in addition to the composited meeting video. Off by default. Set it to `true` when you need one file for each participant. On Google Meet, `video_separate_streams: true` also needs `video_required: true`. Otherwise the request returns `400`.

live_audio_required.description: WebSocket URL to stream live audio output from the meeting.

live_video_required.description: Reserved outbound meeting-video configuration. Google Meet, Zoom and Teams meeting bots accept it but ignore it (no live video is sent, and the bot runs on the larger video tier). Only Zoom Meeting Direct Connect (RTMS) sessions stream live video.

bot_camera_stream.description: Inbound WebRTC video and optional audio published through the bot's camera and microphone. Supported on Google Meet, Teams, and Zoom. Zoom does not allow agent_config_id with this field. Teams and Zoom require a public wss:// signaling URL. See the Bot Camera Streaming guide.
